findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is null/empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: In `EventManager.create`, the Google Meet fallback check was changed from `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` (null-safe) to `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. When the event has no destination calendar (which is common — `handleNewBooking` now sets `destinationCalendar: null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one) and the location is Meet, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and reading `.integration` throws a TypeError, crashing booking creation. The optional chaining on the destructured value was lost.

findings.title: Team destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists. A few lines later, collective team members' calendars are added via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` — the optional chaining means the push is a no-op when the value is `null`, so all collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded. For a collective event whose organizer has no destination calendar but whose hosts do, no host receives a calendar event, which is exactly the bug this PR is meant to fix. The array should be initialized (e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`).

findings.title: Office365 createEvent always uses the main host's calendar ID, breaking other hosts
findings.body: With `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now creating one event per destination calendar using each host's own credential, `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` still takes only the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) and posts to `/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId}/events`. When this service instance belongs to a non-main host, that externalId is the main host's calendar ID, which does not exist in the team member's Office365 account, so creation fails (404) and that host never gets the event. Unlike the Google service, no matching by `credentialId` was added here.

findings.title: Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar regardless of credential
findings.body: Same class of bug as Office365: `createEvent` (and `createAttendees`, `updateEvent`, `deleteEvent`) destructures only the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar`. Since `EventManager` now invokes `createEvent` once per host destination calendar with that host's credential, a Lark credential belonging to a non-main host will attempt to create the event in the main host's Lark calendar ID, which is not accessible/existent for that host's account, so the event creation fails for every non-primary host.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent silently creates nothing for non-main hosts
findings.body: In `BaseCalendarService.createEvent`, the calendar list is filtered by `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` where `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar`. When this service runs with a team member's CalDAV credential (per the new per-host creation loop in EventManager), the main host's calendar URL will not match any of the member's calendars, so the filtered array is empty, `Promise.all([])` succeeds, and the method returns a success result with a uid even though no event was written anywhere. This silently reports success while creating no calendar event for that host.

findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback can never match, leaving calendarId undefined
findings.body: In `updateEvent` the fallback was changed from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. This branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the find predicate compares each calendar's externalId against a falsy value and can never match — `selectedCalendar` is always `undefined`, and `calendarId: selectedCalendar` is passed to `calendar.events.update`, producing an API error and failing the update for any booking reference lacking `externalCalendarId`. The same dead fallback exists in `deleteEvent` (line ~317), where it now falls through to "primary" instead of the event's actual destination calendar, so deletes can target the wrong calendar.

findings.title: createEvent patch uses possibly-undefined calendarId after inserting into primary
findings.body: In `createEvent`, the insert falls back to `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` (used to add the hangout link to the description) still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` unmodified. When no destination calendar matches the credential (selectedCalendar is undefined), the event is created in the primary calendar but the patch request is issued with an undefined calendarId, so the hangout-link patch fails — and since the promise is not awaited or caught, it can also surface as an unhandled rejection.

findings.title: Recurring-cancel deletion now runs once per calendar reference and only cleans the first reference of other bookings
findings.body: The recurring-event deletion block (`if (bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && ... allRemainingBookings)`) was moved inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop, so for a booking with N calendar references (now normal with multiple hosts) the entire recurring-deletion routine executes N times, issuing duplicate deletes of the same events. Additionally, within that block each updated recurring booking is processed via `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`, which only returns the first calendar reference — the other hosts' calendar events on those recurring instances are never deleted, leaving orphaned events in their calendars after a full-series cancellation.

findings.title: Unrelated change inverts IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition for org slug
findings.body: This PR flips `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` (and similarly for `requestedSlug`) in the organization create handler — a semantic inversion unrelated to the destinationCalendar change. With the new condition, the org's `slug` is only written when team billing is enabled and is omitted when it is disabled (previously the opposite), so organizations created on instances without team billing will be missing their slug.

findings.title: loadUsers no longer selects organization.slug for dynamic user list
findings.body: The rewritten `loadUsers` for dynamic group bookings drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the prisma select. Any downstream code that reads `user.organization.slug` for these users (e.g. booker URL / organization subdomain handling) will now receive `undefined`, silently changing behavior for dynamic bookings belonging to organization users. If the removal was intentional it should be verified against all consumers of the loaded users.
